jobs.description:
Director of Engineering

Platform, Infrastructure & Applications | Boston, hybrid | Resonata

About Resonata
Resonata is a precision patient-treatment matching platform. We connect patients with chronic conditions and cancer to the approved treatments and clinical trials they qualify for, and we give biopharma a pay-for-performance channel to reach verified-eligible patients. The matching is deterministic and auditable, grounded in clinical eligibility logic rather than model inference.

The platform is live across 17 indications and roughly 450 treatment options. In head-to-head benchmarking against the leading frontier models, our engine surfaced 92% of confirmed useful care options, three to four times the rate of the models, at 1.47 milliseconds per patient. We have been accepted into two competitive accelerator programs beginning in September.

The role
We are hiring a hands-on Director of Engineering to own the Resonata platform end to end. Most of it is built and running. What it needs now is a single technical owner who can take stewardship of the whole system, harden it, scale it, and keep shipping while we bring it to market.

This is a small team. You are the engineering function, not a manager of one. You write code every day, you make the architectural calls, and you are accountable for what runs in production. You will work alongside two experienced product leaders who own the patient and industry sides of the product, and you will report to the CEO.

One boundary worth stating plainly: the clinical eligibility logic and the analytic system that produces match results sit with the CEO. What you own is how that system is invoked and operated, the pipeline calls and the deployment architecture around them, and whether the whole thing runs reliably and fast at the volumes our partners need.

What you'll own
The whole platform.
Data pipeline operation, database and computing infrastructure, and the applications: the patient web application, the sponsor workbench, and the enroller workbench. One owner, one accountable line.
Production.
Reliability, performance, cost, and security of a system that handles protected health information. Uptime is not someone else's job.
The codebase you inherit.
A meaningful portion of the platform was built by a long-standing engineering partner who is transitioning off. You get a supported handoff from the people who wrote it, not an orphaned repository, and then you decide what to keep, refactor, or replace.
Scale readiness.
We are moving from proving the engine to running it for partners at volume. A million patients should clear the full care-option library in about twenty-five minutes on one machine. Keeping that true as the system grows is yours.
Delivery cadence.
You set how work gets planned, built, reviewed, and released with the product leads. You decide where to use external or AI-assisted resources to move faster, and you manage them.
The team that comes next.
Post-financing, you hire and lead the first engineers. You surface and justify what the team needs before you need it.

Your first ninety days
Complete the handoff of the existing platform, with its original engineers available to you, and reach the point where you can modify any part of it without help.
Establish a deployment, monitoring, and incident practice you would defend in a customer security review.
Ship alongside the product leads through two accelerator programs, without slowing either down.
Give us a clear-eyed technical assessment: what is solid, what is fragile, what has to change before we scale, and what it costs.

Must have
You are genuinely hands-on.
You are writing production code now, not reviewing other people's. If your last two years were roadmaps and headcount, this is not the right fit.
Breadth across the stack.
Python and data pipelines, cloud infrastructure and databases, and modern web applications. You do not need to be the deepest expert in all three, but you have to be dangerous in each and unafraid of the ones you are weakest in.
You inherit well.
You have taken over a system you did not build, under time pressure, and made it yours. You extend an existing architecture on its own terms before deciding it needs replacing.
Correctness discipline.
Our output is a claim about what a patient is eligible for. You test to find your own defects, you root-cause rather than patch, and you treat a silent wrong answer as worse than a loud failure.
Judgment about what to build.
At this stage, most of the leverage is in choosing what not to build. You are decisive about scope and comfortable being the person who says so.
Eight or more years of engineering experience,
including ownership of a production system end to end.

Nice to have
Health data experience: HIPAA, EHR integration, FHIR, or clinical data models.
Building on LLM-assisted pipelines feeding deterministic logic.
Early-stage startup experience, particularly as the first or second engineer.
Two-sided marketplace or B2B SaaS platforms.

Location and commitment
This role is based in Boston, working at least part-time from our office with our product leaders. The proximity matters right now: the fastest path through the next six months runs through people in a room together, deciding quickly.

Compensation
We will be straightforward about this, because you should be able to decide quickly whether it works for you.

Equity until we raise.
This position is equity-compensated until we close our current financing round, at which point it converts to a full-time role at a market salary. The conversion trigger is defined in writing in the offer, not left to judgment later.
A meaningful grant.
Sized for the seniority of the role and for the risk you are taking by joining before the round closes. Our product leaders have been on the same terms since January.
Why now is different.
We have benchmark results that hold up against frontier models, two accelerator acceptances, and materially warmer investor conversations than six months ago. We think this is the inflection point. We are telling you plainly that it is still a bet.

Why this matters
Forty million people a day ask an AI assistant about their health. People with rare and chronic conditions routinely stay on treatments they could have moved off, unaware of approved therapies and open trials they already qualify for. The failures are ordinary and checkable against the patient's own record: a trial closed to enrollment, a site on another continent, a drug the patient already took.

That is an engineering problem with ethical weight to it. The engine that answers it exists and it works. We are reinforcing it to scale and to have lasting impact. If that appeals, reach out!

jobs.title: Senior Director, Engineering - Supply Chain Product Engineering
jobs.description:
Overview

North America Supply Chain is moving from a traditional enterprise technology model to an empowered product operating model. Product Management, Design, and Data capabilities are being established; now we need an engineering leader to build the product engineering capability that brings the model to life at scale.

This is a hands-on build-and-transform leadership mandate, not a traditional systems-administration role focused on building the engineering organization behind North America Supply Chain. Reporting to the Head of Engineering & Platform for North America, you will build and lead the supply chain engineering team responsible for the products that power planning, sourcing, manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and fulfillment.

Our supply chain spans company-owned plants, co-manufacturing partners, suppliers, and distribution networks, creating significant operational complexity. Your mandate is to build high-performing, product-minded engineering teams that modernize critical systems, improve visibility and decision-making, and deliver measurable business outcomes.

What you will own

Supply chain engineering build-out. Build the engineering team, operating rhythms, technical standards, and management practices needed to support a modern product operating model within supply chain. Hire, coach, and develop engineering managers, senior engineers, architects, and product-minded teams capable of owning complex supply chain products and platforms end to end. 
Organization stewardship. Own engineering capacity, talent strategy, partner/vendor decisions, and engineering investment trade-offs. Partner with Product and business leaders to align engineering capacity to the highest-value Supply Chain outcomes while increasing internal capability and improving delivery economics.
Domain-specific technical leadership. Partner with supply chain product, design, data, operations, and business leaders to translate operational priorities into durable technical capabilities. Focus engineering energy on the systems and workflows that matter most across planning, manufacturing, logistics, quality, warehousing, fulfillment, and customer service workflows. 
Product-engineering partnership. Operate as the senior engineering counterpart to supply chain product leadership. Ensure engineers participate early in discovery, shape feasibility and sequencing, and stay accountable for outcomes rather than handoffs or outputs. 
Engineering excellence. Establish standards and metrics for reliability, deployment frequency, cycle time, quality, security, observability, incident learning, and measurable business impact. Make technical debt visible as an operational and business trade-off, not just an engineering concern. 
AI, automation, and engineering productivity. Use AI, automation, integration patterns, and platform engineering to improve developer productivity, supply chain decision quality, workflow automation, and service experiences. Establish responsible guardrails for data readiness, controls, security, compliance, and human-in-the-loop decisioning. 
Portfolio and enterprise leadership. Translate architecture, reliability, delivery, and investment choices into clear business risk and opportunity. Partner with the Head of Engineering and NAOU leaders to align roadmap, funding, headcount, vendor strategy, and platform priorities. 
Capability Transition. Build a deliberate mix of internal and partner engineering capability, using external talent to accelerate delivery while systematically increasing critical engineering knowledge and ownership within TCCC.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related technical field 
12+ years of software, platform, or enterprise engineering experience, including 5+ years leading managers or multi-team engineering organizations
Proven track record building and scaling engineering teams, including defining the hiring bar, team topology, technical standards, operating rhythms, and leadership expectations. 
Experience delivering engineering solutions for supply chain, manufacturing, logistics, fulfillment, operations, or similar 
Strong technical background in modern enterprise architecture, including distributed systems, API and integration platforms, data pipelines or data products, cloud-native architectures, observability, and secure software delivery. 
Experience modernizing legacy, vendor-heavy, or highly integrated systems while maintaining business continuity, using pragmatic build, buy, and partner decisions. 
Demonstrated ability to partner with Product Management, Design, Data, Operations, and business leaders to move from project-based delivery to outcome-oriented product engineering. 
Experience leading multi-domain engineering portfolios with competing priorities, complex dependencies, and senior stakeholder needs. 
Strong understanding of supply chain performance drivers, including service levels, OTIF, inventory, capacity, throughput, quality, logistics, and operational resilience. 
Proven ability to develop engineering leaders, align cross-functional stakeholders, and navigate complex organizational dynamics with clarity, accountability, and inclusion. 

Preferred

Advanced degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Analytics, or Business Administration. 
Experience in CPG, manufacturing, retail, logistics, industrial technology, or other large-scale operational environments. 
Experience working within ERP-enabled supply chain environments, including SAP S/4HANA or equivalent enterprise platforms. 
Familiarity with manufacturing execution systems, warehouse management systems, transportation management systems, or supply chain planning tools such as Blue Yonder, o9, Kinaxis, or similar. 
Experience with real-time data streaming, IoT or manufacturing data, data platforms, analytics, AI, or automation used to improve operational decision-making. 
Experience leading digital or product-model transformation within a large, matrixed, multi-geography enterprise.

Builder Leadership Creates and scales high-performing engineering organizations through strong talent, clear standards, and a culture of accountability.
Technical Judgment Makes sound architectural, platform, and investment decisions that balance speed, quality, risk, and long-term sustainability.
Enterprise Influence Builds alignment across Product, Data, Operations, and Business leaders to drive shared outcomes and priorities.
Transformational Leadership Leads through ambiguity and change, modernizing legacy environments while maintaining business continuity.
Operational Impact Connects technology investments to measurable supply chain outcomes including service, productivity, quality, and resilience.
Product Mindset

Brings engineering into discovery early, challenges assumptions with technical insight, and builds teams accountable for improving outcomes over time rather than simply delivering requirements.

Itron is innovating new ways for utilities and cities to manage energy and water. We create a more resourceful world to protect essential resources for today and tomorrow. Join us.

The Global Test Engineering Manager leads the global test engineering function and is responsible for defining and executing the strategy, development, deployment, standardization, and continuous improvement of manufacturing test solutions across New Product Introduction (NPI) and sustaining product programs. This leader enables high-quality, reliable, and cost-effective test systems that support product performance, manufacturing excellence, operational efficiency, and data-driven decision-making across global operations.

The ideal candidate is a customer-centric and collaborative leader who brings deep technical expertise in electronics manufacturing test engineering, fosters innovation, drives accountability, and thrives in a fast-paced global environment supporting utility and energy technology solutions.

Duties & Responsibilities

Develop and execute a global test engineering strategy aligned with product development, manufacturing, and operations roadmaps.
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing global team of test, automation, and manufacturing engineers, fostering an inclusive culture built on collaboration, accountability, and continuous learning.
Ensure test readiness throughout all phases of New Product Introduction (NPI), including prototype, beta, pilot, and production ramp activities.
Partner with Product Engineering, Quality, Operations, and Supply Chain teams to deliver scalable, reliable, and customer-focused test solutions that support successful product launches and ongoing manufacturing performance.
Drive early engagement in Design for Test (DFT), manufacturability assessments, risk mitigation planning, and product validation activities to improve product quality and operational outcomes.
Lead structured problem-solving efforts, root cause analysis, and corrective actions to resolve test-related issues during development and production.
Establish and maintain global standards for test platforms, architectures, fixtures, automation frameworks, and engineering processes across internal manufacturing sites and external manufacturing partners.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on test coverage, yield improvement, cycle time reduction, capital efficiency, and overall test performance.
Enable robust test data collection, traceability, analytics, and reporting capabilities that support informed decision-making and integration with factory systems.
Evaluate emerging technologies, tools, and methodologies to promote innovation and strengthen manufacturing competitiveness.
Manage budgets, capital expenditure (CAPEX) planning, equipment strategy, supplier relationships, and external engineering partnerships related to test systems and infrastructure.
Influence cross-functional stakeholders and provide technical leadership to align test engineering priorities with business objectives.
Support global manufacturing operations with an agile mindset while maintaining a strong focus on safety, quality, delivery, and customer satisfaction.
Champion a culture of technical excellence, authenticity, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement across the organization.

Required Skills & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
10+ years of progressive experience in electronics manufacturing test engineering, including responsibility for complex products and manufacturing environments.
7+ years of leadership experience managing global, multi-site, or geographically distributed engineering teams.
Demonstrated experience developing and implementing global test engineering strategies and organizational roadmaps.
Strong expertise in In-Circuit Test (ICT), Functional Test, System-Level Test, Reliability Test, and manufacturing test methodologies.
Deep knowledge of Automated Test Equipment (ATE), fixture design, hardware/software integration, test automation, and manufacturing test architectures.
Experience programming and developing automated test solutions using Python, LabVIEW, C#, or similar tools.
Strong understanding of hardware validation, RF testing principles, data acquisition, and test system performance optimization.
Experience supporting high-volume manufacturing operations and working with Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) partners.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, influence stakeholders, and drive measurable business outcomes.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills with experience translating complex technical challenges into scalable solutions.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills with the ability to effectively engage global teams and diverse stakeholders.
Demonstrated commitment to customer-centricity, accountability, collaboration, agility, and innovation.

Preferred Skills & Experience

Master’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Business Administration, or a related field.
Experience supporting connected devices, communication technologies, smart infrastructure, utility, energy, industrial, or IoT products.
Knowledge of manufacturing quality systems, statistical process control, reliability engineering, and failure analysis methodologies.
Experience implementing digital manufacturing, Industry 4.0, test analytics, or factory data integration solutions.
Six Sigma Green Belt, Six Sigma Black Belt, Lean Manufacturing, or similar continuous improvement certification.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
Experience leading global standardization initiatives across multiple manufacturing sites and contract manufacturing partners.
Familiarity with regulatory, compliance, and quality requirements applicable to utility, energy, and industrial technology products.

Benefits Info

This position also includes a competitive benefit package including; financial, social, health and wellbeing programs, paid vacation, 401k matching, employee stock purchase program, hybrid work schedule, and more!

The Role

Convera is a leading B2B cross-border payments company. Our data sits across a legacy platform, an operational data store, and a long tail of source systems. Bringing it into a single governed store is one of the central commitments in our go-forward plan - it is what reporting, analytics, and effectively every AI initiative in the company are currently waiting on.

This role owns Data Engineering, Solution Data Architecture, and Data Science, and is accountable for delivering Convera's enterprise data platform while ensuring continuity of existing operational and regulatory workloads throughout the transformation.Your responsible for modernizing the enterprise data estate by progressively migrating legacy reporting platforms (including DataHub and, over time, ODS) to the Convera Enterprise Data Platform (CEDP), enabling trusted reporting, analytics, AI and regulatory capabilities on a unified foundation. Your first job is to take hold of an in-flight transformation without dropping it. Your second is to finish it, leaving behind a data estate that stands up to regulators, auditors and supports enterprise AI.

What You'll Own

Deliver the single data store. Consolidate Convera's data into one governed platform that reporting, analytics, and AI enablement all build on. The target platform has been selected; your job is execution, not another evaluation cycle.
Lead the phased migration from legacy reporting platforms to the enterprise data platform while maintaining uninterrupted business and regulatory operations.
Hold the committed roadmap. Take over an in-flight program with milestones already communicated. Continuity comes first - sustain delivery, then raise the bar. Renegotiating the plan is an option of last resort, and you will be expected to say so early if it becomes one.
Run the ODS and decide its future. Keep the operational data store stable and feeding transactional systems throughout the migration - this is a run responsibility, not a legacy footnote - and make and defend the call on what happens to it when the target platform lands.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture on enterprise-wide data standards, canonical models, reference architecture, information models and technology strategy. Clearly define operating boundaries between Enterprise Data Architecture and Solution Data Architecture.
Build the pipelines. ETL and ELT at scale out of a complex legacy estate, including streaming pipelines for real-time data movement, with reconciliation to source, monitoring, and recovery that hold up under scrutiny. Data movement that fails quietly is worse than data movement that fails loudly.
Own data science. Set direction for analytical and machine learning work that changes decisions - pricing and margin, risk, client behavior - and partner with Risk and Compliance on model governance so what you build is defensible as well as accurate.
Own governance, quality, and stewardship. Definitions, lineage, ownership, and quality service levels that the business trusts because they match what it experiences. Governance is something people run, not something they read. Establish clear ownership, lineage, definitions and quality standards that the business trusts and actively uses. Partner to ensure that governance accelerates delivery, not become administrative overhead.
Protect the data by design. Secure storage, encryption, masking and tokenization, access control, and retention across every jurisdiction we operate in - built into the platform rather than bolted on when someone asks.
Stand in front of regulators and auditors. Convera is regulated in multiple markets. You will be the person who explains the data estate to an examiner or an auditor, and who stands behind the answer.
Serve the rest of the business. Dashboards and reporting sit elsewhere today; collaborate with the teams that own them and give them governed, documented, well-modeled data instead of extracts and goodwill. Build and maintain a searchable data catalog that makes self-serve discovery realistic rather than aspirational.
Build toward data as a product. There is no client-facing data offering today, but there will be an opportunity once the estate is in order - including democratized data APIs that surface Convera's data externally. Architect with that in mind rather than retrofitting it later.
Lead the organization. Assess the talent and the technology honestly, reshape the team where it needs reshaping, and set an operating cadence that holds delivery steady while you do it. Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Operations, Finance, Risk and Compliance to ensure data priorities align with enterprise outcomes.

What You Bring

15+ years in data, including 8+ years in management and the senior-most data role (VP Data, Head of Data, or CDO) at a fintech, payments, or regulated financial services company.
Delivered a consolidated data platform end to end - from a fragmented legacy estate to a single governed store the business actually uses. Modern cloud data warehouse experience (Snowflake, Databricks, or comparable) required.
Deep data engineering credentials: large-scale ETL and ELT, pipeline reliability, reconciliation, and performance in environments where the source systems are neither clean nor cooperative.
Data governance in practice - lineage, definitions, stewardship, and quality - installed and sustained, not documented and abandoned.
Data privacy and secure data handling at depth: encryption, masking and tokenization, access control, and retention obligations across multiple jurisdictions.
Direct experience with regulators, examiners, and auditors - you have been in the room and answered the questions yourself.
Leadership spanning data engineering, architecture, and data science, including production machine learning that served real decisions rather than a research backlog. Hands-on experience preparing data for ML: labeling, feature engineering, and creating training-ready assets at scale.
A transformation track record: taken over an existing organization, assessed talent and technology candidly, and turned it into an accountable team without stalling committed delivery.
Cross-border payments, FX, or treasury data experience a plus; PE-backed environment a plus.
Bachelor's degree required.

First 12 Months, If You're The One

The committed milestones met rather than renegotiated. A single governed store with the priority domains landed and reconciled to source. The ODS stable, and its future decided rather than deferred. Definitions and quality the business trusts enough to stop keeping its own copy of the numbers. A data estate that survives an examiner or an audit without a scramble. And an AI agenda that is no longer waiting on data readiness.

About Convera

Convera is a global leader in commercial payments that powers international business by moving money with ease. We provide tech-led payment solutions to help more than 26,000 customers globally grow with confidence, from small businesses to CFOs and treasurers. As experts in foreign exchange, risk and compliance, with an unrivaled regulatory footprint, Convera’s financial network spans more than 140 currencies and 200 countries and territories.

Our teams care deeply about the value we deliver to our customers, which makes Convera a rewarding place to work. This is an exciting time for our organization as we expand our team with growth-minded, results-oriented people who are looking to move fast in an innovative environment.

Your Role

The Stellarus Technology team builds and operates the platform, services, and products that support payer operations, member experiences, customer integrations, and internal product delivery. You will work directly with developers to define the standards, patterns, tooling, and expectations teams use when they design, build, test, and operate services, including where AI and AI-assisted engineering tools can improve quality, speed, and signal.

Your Work

Lead incident and launch readiness reviews where performance, scalability, or reliability risk is material.
Mentor developers, architects, and managers on performance design, test automation, failure analysis, and production readiness.
Build a small high-leverage team over time, while remaining close enough to the tooling and technical details to set direction credibly.
